engagement_summary.production_method: Controlled hydroponic cultivation of Lemna minor in enclosed greenhouse raceway ponds, followed by mechanical maceration, green/white fraction separation, calcium chloride coagulation of chlorophyll, microfiltration (0.2 µm), and ultrafiltration (70 kDa membrane), then drying
engagement_summary.target_population: General US population 2 years and older; excludes infants, toddlers in infant formula, and meat/poultry products under USDA jurisdiction
engagement_summary.dietary_exposure_method: NHANES WWEIA 2017-2020 pre-pandemic 24-hour dietary recall data; FNDDS ingredient fractionation; DaDiet software; eaters-only and per capita estimates stratified by age and sex
engagement_summary.submission_completeness_note: The notice includes Parts I–VII with appendices covering specifications, batch analyses, dietary intake, allergenicity, regulatory status, and an expert panel statement. The manufacturing process description is present but lacks full detail on processing aids and nutrient media composition.

categorical_eligibility.basis: LLP is a plant-derived protein concentrate intended as a food ingredient; it is not a food additive requiring premarket approval if GRAS criteria are met under 21 CFR 170.30(a) and (b). The substance is not a color additive, dietary supplement under DSHEA, or drug.

scope_clarity.notes: Food categories are mapped to 21 CFR 170.3(n) definitions with use levels of 1–20%. Technical functions include nutritional protein source, emulsifier, and gelation/thickening agent. Standard of Identity limitations are acknowledged.

existing_regulatory_status.prior_gras_notices: GRN 742 (Parabel Ltd, LENTEIN Complete, Lemnaceae protein powder) — FDA issued No Questions letter August 22, 2018. This notice is the primary regulatory anchor.
existing_regulatory_status.food_additive_approvals: None identified for LLP specifically. Rubisco (CAS 9027-23-0) has no standalone food additive approval.
existing_regulatory_status.notes: EFSA approved water lentil protein concentrate from L. minor and L. gibba (ABC Kroos BV) in April 2023. EFSA declined to establish safety for Parabel's LENTEIN Complete and Wolffia globosa Mankai powder due to manganese levels — a distinction the submission addresses by demonstrating LLP manganese at ~11.4 ppm vs. 128–333 ppm in Parabel's product.

potential_safety_signals.signal: Batch 4 aerobic plate count (22,000 CFU/g) exceeds specification of <15,000 CFU/g
potential_safety_signals.evidence: Table 3 (Appendix 1, Batch 4, Lot P030122C1) shows APC of 22,000 CFU/g against a specification of <15,000 CFU/g. No explanation or corrective action is provided in the submission.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Provide explanation for the out-of-specification result, document investigation and corrective action, and confirm whether this lot was released or rejected. Demonstrate that the specification is achievable and consistently met.

potential_safety_signals.signal: EFSA identified treatment-related findings in the Wolffia globosa 90-day rat study that the submission characterizes as non-adverse
potential_safety_signals.evidence: EFSA (2021c) concluded the NOAEL for the Mankai 90-day study was 6.5 g/kg bw/day (males), not 13.16 g/kg bw/day as stated by the submitter. The submission adopts the higher NOAEL without adequately addressing EFSA's contrary interpretation.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Reconcile the NOAEL discrepancy with EFSA's published opinion. Calculate a margin of exposure using the more conservative EFSA NOAEL (6.5 g/kg bw/day) against the 90th percentile EDI (1.0 g/kg bw/day) and discuss adequacy.

potential_safety_signals.signal: Read-across from GRN 742 toxicology data to a substantially more concentrated product without bridging toxicology
potential_safety_signals.evidence: LLP is ≥80% protein (as-is) vs. LENTEIN Complete at 39–55% protein (dw). The fiber content differs substantially (NMT 15% vs. 30–45% dw). No new in vivo toxicology was conducted on LLP itself.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Strengthen the compositional bridging argument with quantitative similarity analysis. Consider whether the higher protein concentration and lower fiber content alter the toxicological profile or exposure to any minor components.

identity_and_characterization.summary: LLP is well-characterized as a ≥80% protein concentrate from Lemna minor, with Rubisco identified as the dominant protein (~60% of total protein by SDS-PAGE). Taxonomic classification, CAS number for Rubisco, physical specifications, and five-batch analytical data are provided. Allergenicity is addressed through an expert opinion (Dr. Gendel) and bioinformatic rationale, though no pepsin digestibility data specific to LLP were generated.

strengths.observation: Five non-consecutive batch analyses demonstrate consistent protein content (80.85–82.56%), low oxalic acid (<0.02%), and heavy metals well within specifications.
Rubisco is identified as the major protein with CAS number, EC number, and mechanistic description; its ubiquity and history of safe consumption in leafy vegetables is well-documented.
strengths.section_reference: Part II, Section 2.7; Part VI, Section 6.2

strengths.observation: Allergenicity assessment by Dr. Gendel (Appendix 6) covers taxonomic relatedness, CFSAN AERS review, and absence of published allergy reports; prior expert opinion from GRN 742 (Dr. Taylor) is incorporated by reference.

gaps.title: No pepsin digestibility data for LLP allergenicity assessment
gaps.observation: The submission acknowledges Rubisco is rapidly degraded by pepsin but cites no actual pepsin digestibility study for LLP. The allergenicity section relies on absence-of-reports and bioinformatic rationale. For a novel protein at up to 20% inclusion, absence of digestibility data is a recognized adequacy gap per corpus analysis (9.5% delta for allergenicity).

gaps.title: Batch 4 out-of-specification APC result unexplained
gaps.observation: Batch 4 APC of 22,000 CFU/g exceeds the 15,000 CFU/g specification. No investigation, corrective action, or disposition of this lot is described. This undermines the claim that LLP consistently meets food-grade specifications.

gaps.title: Fat content not measured in five-batch analysis
gaps.observation: Total fat was not measured in any of the five batches; the submission notes fat meets <0.5% specification based on 'other analyses' (Appendix 2). A single representative CoA is insufficient to demonstrate batch-to-batch consistency for a specification parameter.

manufacturing_process.summary: A schematic process flow (Figure 2) and narrative description are provided covering cultivation, harvest, maceration, green/white fraction separation, calcium chloride coagulation, microfiltration, ultrafiltration, and drying. The description is adequate at a high level but lacks specificity on nutrient media composition, processing aid quantities, and validation of contaminant removal.

strengths.observation: The submission identifies all major unit operations including 0.2 µm microfiltration and 70 kDa ultrafiltration steps specifically designed to remove heavy metals and contaminants.
strengths.section_reference: Part II, Section 2.5; Part VI, Section 6.3.3

strengths.observation: cGMP compliance, SQF Level 2 Category 19, and 21 CFR 117 adherence are stated; all processing aids are described as food-grade with a history of use in food processing.
strengths.section_reference: Part II, Section 2.5; Part VI, Section 6.6

gaps.title: Nutrient media composition not disclosed
gaps.observation: The submission states nutrients are added to optimize growth but does not identify the specific nutrient media components. For an aquatic plant grown in controlled ponds, media composition is relevant to assessing potential carry-over of nitrogen sources, phosphates, or other components into the finished product.

gaps.title: Processing aid identity and quantities not specified
gaps.observation: Calcium chloride is identified as the coagulant but no quantities, grades, or residual levels in the finished product are provided. Other processing aids are described only generically as 'food grade.' FDA typically expects identification of all processing aids and their regulatory status.

gaps.title: No validation data for contaminant removal by filtration steps
gaps.observation: The submission asserts that microfiltration and ultrafiltration remove heavy metals and contaminants but provides no validation data demonstrating removal efficiency. The batch data show heavy metals well within limits, which provides indirect support, but process validation is not documented.

dietary_exposure.summary: The EDI assessment uses NHANES WWEIA 2017-2020 pre-pandemic data with FNDDS ingredient fractionation and DaDiet software, covering all proposed food categories. The 90th percentile user intake for ages 2+ is 61.1 g/day (1.0 g/kg bw/day); children 1–5 years show the highest intake at 2.7 g/kg bw/day. The methodology is generally sound and consistent with FDA expectations.

strengths.observation: NHANES WWEIA 2017-2020 pre-pandemic data used with FNDDS ingredient fractionation for mixed dishes — appropriate methodology that avoids overestimation from applying use levels to whole food weights.
Age-stratified results including children 1–5 years (highest exposure at 2.7 g/kg bw/day at 90th percentile) are presented, addressing the most sensitive subpopulation within the intended use scope.
The submission contextualizes LLP EDI against GRN 742's budget-type analysis (27.8–55.6 g/person/day) and notes LLP EDI is comparable, supporting the adequacy of the GRN 742 safety database.

gaps.title: Minor discrepancy between summary table and appendix EDI values
gaps.section_reference: Part III, Table 10 vs. Appendix 3, Table 3
gaps.observation: Table 10 reports 90th percentile for ages 2+ as 61.1 g/day, while Appendix 3 Table 3 shows per capita 90th percentile of 69.5 g/day and per user 90th percentile of 61.1 g/day. The distinction between per capita and per user is not clearly explained in the main text, which could cause confusion about the appropriate exposure estimate.

gaps.title: No acute/single-serving exposure analysis
gaps.observation: At up to 20% inclusion in plant protein products, a single serving could deliver a substantial bolus of LLP. No acute exposure estimate is provided. Given the 90-day NOAEL from gavage studies (1,000 mg/kg bw/day for LENTEIN Complete), a single-serving analysis would strengthen the safety margin characterization.

safety_data.summary: The safety case relies primarily on read-across from GRN 742 (LENTEIN Complete) toxicology data, supplemented by a 90-day rat study with Wolffia globosa Mankai powder, in vitro genotoxicity data (Ames + micronucleus on Mankai), and multiple human clinical studies with L. minor and Wolffia. No in vivo toxicology was conducted on LLP itself. The genotoxicity battery is complete for the analog substance. The NOAEL discrepancy with EFSA for the Mankai study is not adequately resolved.

strengths.observation: Genotoxicity battery for Wolffia globosa Mankai includes both Ames test (OECD 471) and in vitro micronucleus test (OECD 487) — a complete two-assay battery with and without metabolic activation.

Three human clinical studies with L. minor (Zeinstra 2019; Mes 2022a; Mes 2022b) demonstrate no adverse effects at single-dose and 11-day repeated consumption, with clinical chemistry, blood pressure, and GI complaint monitoring.

Manganese content of LLP (~11.4 ppm) is approximately 20-fold lower than Parabel's LENTEIN Complete (128–333 ppm), directly addressing the EFSA safety concern that prevented EU approval of the Parabel product.
strengths.section_reference: Part VI, Section 6.3.3; Part II, Section 2.4

gaps.title: NOAEL discrepancy with EFSA for Mankai 90-day study not resolved
gaps.observation: The submission adopts a NOAEL of 13.16 g/kg bw/day (males) for the Mankai 90-day study. EFSA (2021c) determined the NOAEL was 6.5 g/kg bw/day based on treatment-related findings at the high dose. The submission dismisses EFSA's interpretation without adequate scientific justification. Using EFSA's NOAEL, the margin of exposure at the 90th percentile EDI (1.0 g/kg bw/day) is 6.5-fold — narrow and requiring discussion.

gaps.title: No in vivo toxicology conducted on LLP itself
gaps.observation: All in vivo toxicology is from LENTEIN Complete (39–55% protein, 30–45% fiber) or Mankai powder. LLP at ≥80% protein and ≤15% fiber is a substantially more concentrated product. The compositional bridging argument in Table 11 is qualitative; no quantitative equivalence analysis or read-across justification framework is applied.

gaps.title: Human clinical studies use fresh L. minor plant material, not LLP concentrate
gaps.observation: The three key human studies used fresh L. minor (170 g FW) or Lemna protein concentrate (64% protein), not Plantible's LLP (≥80% protein). The maximum protein dose in human studies (~20 g protein) is substantially below the 90th percentile EDI of 61.1 g LLP/day (~49 g protein). The extrapolation is not explicitly justified.

general_availability.summary: The submission relies on peer-reviewed published literature for the safety case, with GRN 742 incorporated by reference. The expert panel statement (Appendix 7) and allergenicity assessment (Appendix 6) are unpublished documents. The toxicology studies from GRN 742 are available through FDA's GRAS notice inventory. All key references appear to be published in accessible journals.

strengths.observation: Core safety studies (GRN 742 toxicology, Kawamata 2020 genotoxicity and 90-day study, Mes 2022a/b, Zeinstra 2019) are published in peer-reviewed journals and publicly accessible.
No data are claimed as trade secret or exempt from disclosure; the submission states all data can be made publicly available.

gaps.title: Expert panel statement is unpublished and cannot independently establish GRAS
gaps.observation: The expert panel consensus statement (Appendix 7) is an unpublished document. Per GRAS standards, unpublished data can corroborate but cannot establish the GRAS conclusion. The submission appropriately bases its conclusion on published literature, with the panel statement as corroboration.

gaps.title: Stein (2022) amino acid digestibility study cited as URL, not peer-reviewed publication
gaps.observation: The PDCAAS estimation relies on ileal digestibility data from Stein (2022) cited as a university website URL, not a peer-reviewed publication. This data point supports a nutritional claim rather than a safety conclusion, but its non-peer-reviewed status should be noted.

general_acceptance.summary: The weight of evidence supports broad expert acceptance for duckweed-derived proteins as food ingredients. FDA's No Questions letter for GRN 742 and EFSA's 2023 approval of water lentil protein concentrate from L. minor/L. gibba (ABC Kroos BV) provide strong regulatory benchmarks. The primary scientific controversy — manganese levels — is resolved for LLP by demonstrated low manganese content. The EFSA NOAEL discrepancy for the Mankai study represents a residual area of potential expert disagreement.

strengths.observation: FDA issued a No Questions letter for GRN 742 (Parabel LENTEIN Complete) in 2018, establishing regulatory precedent for Lemnaceae protein in food at 1–24 g/serving.
strengths.section_reference: Part VI, Section 6.5; Part II, Section 2.1

strengths.observation: EFSA (2023) approved water lentil protein concentrate from L. minor and L. gibba (ABC Kroos BV) as a novel food — the most directly comparable regulatory action to LLP.
No published reports of adverse effects or allergic reactions to duckweed protein in humans; long history of consumption in Southeast Asia documented across multiple independent sources.
strengths.section_reference: Part III, Section 3.1; Part VI, Section 6.4.4

gaps.title: EFSA's contrary NOAEL interpretation not addressed as a scientific controversy
gaps.observation: EFSA's determination of a lower NOAEL (6.5 g/kg bw/day) for the Mankai 90-day study represents a published, authoritative body finding that contradicts the submission's safety margin calculation. The submission does not acknowledge this as a point of scientific disagreement or provide a reasoned rebuttal.

conditions_of_use.summary: Conditions of use are well-specified with food categories mapped to 21 CFR 170.3(n) definitions, use levels of 1–20% by food category, and technical functions identified. Infant formula and USDA-regulated meat/poultry products are explicitly excluded. Standard of Identity limitations are acknowledged.

strengths.observation: Table 9 provides specific use levels by food category (e.g., 4.1% in beverages, up to 20% in plant protein products), enabling meaningful exposure assessment and comparison to safety data.
Infant formula and toddler foods are explicitly excluded from intended uses, appropriately limiting exposure for the most vulnerable population.
strengths.section_reference: Part I, Section 1.4; Part III, Section 3.2

gaps.title: Standard of Identity conflict not resolved for specific food categories
gaps.section_reference: Part I, Section 1.4; Part III, Section 3.2
gaps.observation: The submission acknowledges Standard of Identity requirements for some food categories but does not identify which specific categories are affected or how the ingredient would be labeled/marketed in those contexts. This is a presentation issue that does not affect the safety case.

regulatory_submission.summary: The submission follows the GRAS notice format with Parts I–VII present. Part I certification is signed by the co-founder of Plantible Foods. The submission incorporates GRN 742 by reference and addresses unfavorable information (EFSA manganese concerns, EFSA NOAEL for Mankai). The expert panel statement in Appendix 7 was truncated in the input provided.

strengths.observation: Part I certification is present and signed, certifying the dossier is complete, representative, and balanced including unfavorable information.
Unfavorable regulatory findings (EFSA rejection of Parabel and Mankai products due to manganese) are disclosed and addressed with LLP-specific manganese data.
strengths.section_reference: Part VI, Section 6.5; Part II, Section 2.4

gaps.title: Expert panel statement content not fully reviewable — truncated in input
gaps.observation: The Appendix 7 expert panel consensus statement was truncated in the input provided. The full document should be verified to confirm panel member qualifications, independence disclosures, scope of review, and whether the panel addressed the EFSA NOAEL discrepancy.

gaps.title: FSIS/USDA notification not applicable but basis for exclusion of meat analogs not fully addressed
gaps.section_reference: Part I, Section 1.11; Part III, Table 9
gaps.observation: Plant protein products include meat imitates at up to 20% LLP. The submission excludes USDA-regulated meat/poultry but does not clarify whether meat analog products (not under USDA jurisdiction) require any additional regulatory consideration.

the leaves of plants, including Lemna minor, in rat diets. Plant samples were collected,
washed, drained, and hand fed into a specialty pulper. The pulper separated the outflow
discharge from the juice of the pulped material. The protein in the juice was precipitated
using steam injection; the subsequent protein coagulum was filtered, washed, pressed, and
freeze-dried. The six experimental diets were prepared with 10% crude protein: a wheat

recommended_next_steps.action: Resolve the EFSA NOAEL discrepancy for the Mankai 90-day rat study. Either provide a detailed scientific rebuttal of EFSA's interpretation of the treatment-related findings, or recalculate the margin of exposure using EFSA's NOAEL of 6.5 g/kg bw/day and demonstrate adequacy at the 90th percentile EDI of 1.0 g/kg bw/day.
recommended_next_steps.gap_title: NOAEL discrepancy with EFSA for Mankai 90-day study not resolved
recommended_next_steps.pushback_reasoning: FDA routinely requests reconciliation when a submission's NOAEL differs from an authoritative body's published determination on the same study, particularly when the margin of exposure at the conservative NOAEL is less than 10-fold.

recommended_next_steps.action: Explain and document the Batch 4 out-of-specification aerobic plate count (22,000 CFU/g vs. <15,000 CFU/g specification). Provide investigation records, corrective action, and lot disposition. Demonstrate that the specification is routinely achievable with additional batch data.
recommended_next_steps.pushback_reasoning: FDA consistently flags OOS results in batch data submitted as evidence of consistent manufacturing; an unexplained OOS result in 1 of 5 batches (20%) directly undermines the consistency claim and is a standard information request trigger.

recommended_next_steps.action: Strengthen the read-across justification from GRN 742 toxicology to LLP by applying a structured read-across framework (e.g., ECHA/EFSA approach) that quantitatively addresses the compositional differences (protein concentration, fiber content) and their potential toxicological relevance. Alternatively, conduct a 28-day repeat-dose study in rats with LLP itself.
recommended_next_steps.gap_title: No in vivo toxicology conducted on LLP itself
recommended_next_steps.pushback_reasoning: FDA has accepted read-across for closely related protein concentrates in prior GRAS notices, but the ~2-fold difference in protein concentration and ~3-fold difference in fiber content between LLP and LENTEIN Complete may prompt a request for additional bridging data or a structured justification.

recommended_next_steps.action: Identify all nutrient media components used in cultivation and all processing aids (including calcium chloride grade, quantity, and residual levels in finished product). Confirm regulatory status of each processing aid under 21 CFR Parts 172, 173, or GRAS.
recommended_next_steps.gap_title: Nutrient media composition and processing aid identity not disclosed
recommended_next_steps.pushback_reasoning: FDA's standard information request for novel food ingredients produced by controlled cultivation includes identification of all growth media components and processing aids, as these can be sources of process-related contaminants not captured by finished product specifications.

recommended_next_steps.action: Conduct or cite a pepsin digestibility study for LLP or a closely matched Lemna protein isolate (≥80% protein) to complete the allergenicity assessment. The current reliance on absence-of-reports and Rubisco's known pepsin susceptibility, while reasonable, does not constitute a formal digestibility assessment for a novel protein at high inclusion levels.
recommended_next_steps.gap_title: No pepsin digestibility data for LLP allergenicity assessment
recommended_next_steps.pushback_reasoning: FDA's allergenicity guidance and the 9.5% corpus delta for allergenicity absence indicate this is a moderate-probability information request, particularly for novel proteins at use levels up to 20% where consumer exposure is substantial.

summary_paragraph:
• Foundational gaps: None identified — the submission has a viable safety foundation anchored by GRN 742 (FDA No Questions, 2018) and EFSA's 2023 approval of L. minor/L. gibba protein concentrate; the absence of LLP-specific in vivo toxicology is a material gap but does not render the submission unsupportable given the compositional similarity argument.
• Material gaps: (1) EFSA's published NOAEL of 6.5 g/kg bw/day for the Mankai 90-day study (Part VI, Section 6.3.3) is not reconciled — the submission adopts 13.16 g/kg bw/day without adequate rebuttal, yielding a potentially narrow margin of exposure; (2) Batch 4 APC of 22,000 CFU/g exceeds specification with no explanation (Part II, Table 3); (3) read-across from LENTEIN Complete (39–55% protein) to LLP (≥80% protein) lacks a structured justification framework; (4) nutrient media and processing aid identities are not disclosed (Part II, Section 2.5); (5) no pepsin digestibility data for allergenicity (Part VI, Section 6.4.4).
• Safety signals: The EFSA NOAEL discrepancy is the most significant signal; the OOS batch result raises manufacturing consistency questions; human clinical studies used lower-concentration products at doses below the 90th percentile EDI.
• Benchmark context: This notice is structurally stronger than GRN 742 in dietary exposure methodology (NHANES vs. budget analysis) and directly addresses the manganese issue that caused EFSA to decline Parabel's EU application; it is comparable to approved aquatic plant protein notices in safety data depth.
• Overall readiness: The submission is substantively viable but requires resolution of the EFSA NOAEL discrepancy and the OOS batch result before filing; the remaining gaps are addressable through additional documentation rather than new studies.
limitations_and_caveats: This assessment is based solely on the document text provided, which was truncated before Appendix 4 (regulatory reviews), Appendix 5 (Rubisco bibliography), and the full content of Appendix 7 (expert panel statement). Gaps classified as documentation_gap with documentation_issue priority in truncated sections may be material if the full document does not contain the expected information. The dietary exposure appendix (Appendix 3) was reviewed in full as provided. No independent literature search was conducted; the assessment relies on citations as represented in the submission. This analysis does not constitute a legal opinion or predict FDA's response to the notice.
